crossStoryFindings: The archive primitive, turn derivation, and derived-view layers are implemented against the full Epic 7 taxonomy, but the live execution/finalization path still feeds them legacy `ProcessHistoryItem` data, so later stories are validated against seeded archive rows instead of the real runtime source.

Story 6 provenance enrichment is disconnected from Stories 2-3 production writes: archive reads can enrich `relatedArtifactVersionId` and `relatedSourceProvenanceId`, but the shipped append paths never persist those IDs.

The archive page, turn page, and derived-view page all work when archive rows already exist, but the default shipped execution flow does not generate the archive shape those stories were designed around.
architectureFindings: `ExecutionResult` is still typed as `processHistoryItems: ProcessHistoryItem[]`, and `ProcessHistoryItem` still exposes the legacy presentation vocabulary rather than the canonical archive taxonomy.

The design contract said archive rows would store nullable artifact/source/tool IDs and read services would enrich later; current checkpoint/provenance interfaces do not return the identifiers needed to realize that contract on the live path.
The process work-surface contract/UI never added the designed archive entry point, so archive/turn/view routes are not connected to the primary process surface.
epicCoverageAssessment: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all` both exited 0.

Automation is masking the main integration gaps: tests such as `tests/service/server/turn-derivation.test.ts` and `tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts` seed canonical archive rows directly, and `tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts` seeds provenance-linked rows directly, instead of proving the live runtime can emit them.

The gate is still lighter than the epic implies: `guard:no-test-changes` prints `SKIP` and `test:e2e` is scaffold-only, so there is no executable end-to-end check for live archive generation or archive navigation.
productionPathFindings: `createApp` wires `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` by default, and that service still uses the documented Epic 3 default placeholder payload; the placeholder emits a synthetic `process_event` plus "Execution placeholder..." side-work output rather than real low-level archive material.

No production archive append path populates `relatedArtifactVersionId`, `relatedSourceProvenanceId`, or `relatedToolCallId`; the live appenders explicitly write those fields as `null`, so provenance and tool-correlation behavior is unreachable from real traffic.

Checkpoint persistence and source-provenance recording happen only after archive finalization and expose no archive-linkable identifiers back to the archive writer, so Story 6 enrichment currently works only for pre-seeded/test-fixture rows.

blockingFindings.title: Live execution cannot emit the Epic 7 archive taxonomy
blockingFindings.evidence: `ProcessHistoryItem` only allows `user_message|process_message|progress_update|attention_request|side_work_update|process_event` in `apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts:124-131`, and `ExecutionResult` still exposes `processHistoryItems: ProcessHistoryItem[]` in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/provider-adapter.ts:125-132`. `ProcessHistoryCompatService` only maps `user_message`, `process_message`, and `process_event` into archive kinds in `apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts:8-23`. On the shipped path, `createApp` defaults to `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` in `apps/platform/server/app.ts:285-286`, and that default service still uses the documented Epic 3 placeholder payload in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:159-177`, which emits only a synthetic `process_event` in `script-execution.service.ts:85-128`. As a result, the runtime cannot produce `reasoning`, `script_emission`, `tool_call`, or `tool_result` archive entries at all, and does not produce real `model_message` traffic without a non-default injected runner.

blockingFindings.title: Archive rows never capture artifact/source provenance on the live path
blockingFindings.evidence: Both live archive appenders hardcode relation fields to `null`: `apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts:39-56` and `apps/platform/server/services/processes/process-response.service.ts:151-167`. During execution, archive finalization happens before provenance recording in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:563-581` and `690-706`; later checkpoint/provenance steps run separately in `process-environment.service.ts:829-882`. Those downstream interfaces do not return linkable identifiers: `persistCheckpointArtifacts` returns only `PlatformProcessOutputSummary[]` in `apps/platform/server/services/projects/platform-store.ts:386-389`, and `SourceProvenanceService.recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources` / `recordReceivedCodeUpdates` both return `Promise<void>` in `apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:22-34`. The read-time enrichment added for Story 6 therefore depends on IDs that production never writes.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Process work surface never exposes an archive entry point
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `renderProcessWorkSurfacePage` accepts callbacks for project, review, start, resume, rehydrate, rebuild, and respond only in `apps/platform/client/features/processes/process-work-surface-page.ts:27-45`, and its control switch has no archive navigation case in `process-work-surface-page.ts:140-169`. The shared control contract likewise only defines `start`, `respond`, `resume`, `rehydrate`, `rebuild`, `review`, and `restart` in `apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts:176-206`. The archive route exists, but it is not discoverable from the primary process surface.

unresolvedItems: `verify-all` passed, but `test:e2e` is scaffold-only and `guard:no-test-changes` is not implemented, so those gate layers remain unproven.
This review did not manually run `pnpm run convex:dev` and `pnpm dev` to validate archive generation against a live backend/provider session.

crossStoryFindings: The route, store, client, and test surfaces for archive/turn/view reads are wired end to end, and both `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all` passed.

Cross-story drift remains between the Story 1/2 write path and the Story 4/5/6 read path: turns, derived views, and provenance enrichment assume a richer canonical archive than the shipped execution path actually produces.
Most low-level archive taxonomy and provenance scenarios are proven with fixtures/in-memory stores rather than by the real execution pipeline.
architectureFindings: The tech design says Fastify should finalize completed model/runtime objects, script emissions, and tool call/result pairs into canonical archive entries, but the implementation still canonicalizes runtime output through presentation-level `processHistoryItems` compatibility mapping.
The design says `archiveTurns` are cached projections for bounded reads, but turn and derived-view GETs rebuild from full archive scans on each request instead of serving cached projections first.

The design expects archive entries to carry nullable artifact/source/tool foreign keys for read-time enrichment, but the shipped writers persist provenance on parallel tables without linking those ids back onto archive rows.
epicCoverageAssessment: Story 3-5 read surfaces are present and exercised by tests, including access control, empty states, degraded rendering, and derived-view conflict handling.

Story 1-2 are only partially realized on the production path: canonical append currently reaches `user_message`, `model_message`, and `process_event`, not the full seven-kind archive taxonomy required by the epic.

Story 6 provenance coherence is implemented as a read-time enrichment layer, but the write path never supplies the archive-side ids that would let real archive entries surface artifact/source provenance.
productionPathFindings: The default execution path still runs the explicit placeholder script payload in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts`, and that payload emits a single finalized `process_event` instead of real low-level reasoning/script/tool archive objects.

Artifact checkpoints and source-provenance records are persisted on side channels, but the shipped archive writers never attach `relatedArtifactVersionId` or `relatedSourceProvenanceId` to canonical archive entries.

Archive source-provenance enrichment only looks at the newest 200 provenance rows for a process, so older archive pages can report healthy links as degraded once real archive rows start linking to older provenance ids.
Turn and derived-view reads currently pay full-archive rebuild cost on every request rather than using cached projections as the primary bounded read path.

blockingFindings.title: The shipped archive write path never produces four of the seven required canonical entry kinds
blockingFindings.evidence: `ExecutionResult` only carries `processHistoryItems`, outputs, side-work writes, and checkpoint candidates (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/provider-adapter.ts:125-132`). `processHistoryItemKindSchema` is limited to `user_message`, `process_message`, `progress_update`, `attention_request`, `side_work_update`, and `process_event` (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts:124-131`). Runtime execution stores those history items and then archives them through `appendFromProcessHistoryItem` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:690-706`), while `ProcessHistoryCompatService` only maps `user_message`, `process_message`, and `process_event` into archive entries and hard-codes the related ids to `null` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts:8-12`, `:39-56`). The default production script payload is still the shared placeholder and only emits a finalized `process_event` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:15-135`, `:158-163`). As shipped, the real path never emits `reasoning`, `script_emission`, `tool_call`, or `tool_result` archive entries.

blockingFindings.title: Archive provenance coherence is unreachable on the real write path because archive rows never record related artifact/source ids
blockingFindings.evidence: Accepted user-response archiving explicitly writes `relatedArtifactVersionId: null` and `relatedSourceProvenanceId: null` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/process-response.service.ts:151-167`). The compatibility archive path also hard-codes all related ids to `null` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts:39-56`). Meanwhile the execution/checkpoint flow persists artifacts and source provenance on separate paths via `persistCheckpointArtifacts`, `recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources`, and `recordReceivedCodeUpdates` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:577-581`, `:830-883`), and `SourceProvenanceService` creates durable provenance rows separately (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:200-218`). Because no shipped archive writer threads those ids back onto archive entries, the Story 6 enrichment surface is only reachable from fixtures/tests, not from real archive data.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Source provenance enrichment can falsely degrade older archive entries because it only loads the newest 200 provenance rows
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `listProcessSourceProvenanceEntries` returns only the 200 most recent source-provenance records for a process (`convex/sourceProvenance.ts:58-71`). `ArchiveReadService` loads that process-wide slice once when any page contains `relatedSourceProvenanceId` values (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts:120-126`) and resolves each entry from that in-memory map (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts:148-160`). If an archive page references an older but still-existing provenance id outside the newest 200 rows, the entry is incorrectly degraded with `Related source provenance is unavailable.` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts:198-200`).

nonBlockingFindings.title: Turn and derived-view reads bypass the cached-projection design and rescan the full archive on every request
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `getTurns` always calls `rebuildTurns` before reading a page (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:61-85`), and `rebuildTurns` paginates through the entire archive (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:89-110`). `listViews` and `refreshViews` likewise rebuild turns and recompute full-archive signatures by scanning all archive entries before responding (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:50-86`, `:100-143`, `:148-182`). Functionally this works, but it drifts from the tech design's cached/bounded projection model for long-running processes.

unresolvedItems: The 2-second performance NFR for turn/archive reads at 5,000 archive entries was not measured against a real Convex-backed runtime during this review.
Manual end-to-end verification with `pnpm run convex:dev` and `pnpm dev` was not performed; production-path conclusions are based on code inspection plus automated test results.
